Case A

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=1

This PR makes the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are its author. That covers what the ticket asks for, and the README describes the behavior correctly.

Nothing needs fixing, but merging waits on one thing: a required unit test check is still running on the commit being reviewed, and the watch window for it ran out. No check has failed, and no approval or other outside step is missing.

I recommend deliver because another watch window can see the still-running unit test check finish.

Pick one:
1. deliver - watch the still-running unit test check for one more window; the repair and sync attempt limits stay as they are. [recommended]
2. assess - end the repair course without posting anything, because there are no problems to post.
3. stop - end the run and leave the PR as it is.

Case D

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR is meant to make the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are its author. That requirement is not covered yet, because the endpoint still returns a fixed version, while the README describes the intended behavior correctly.

One problem blocks merging. The health endpoint returns a version written into the code instead of the version of the build that is running, so a deployed service can report the wrong version (src/health.ts:8). The health_version test in tests/health.test.mjs failed locally for this reason.

I recommend deliver because the drafted repair reads the existing build-version value and you can push it.

Pick one:
1. deliver - repair blockers, rebase on main, watch CI, repeat until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review and make no repairs.
3. stop - end the run and leave the PR as it is.

Case E

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR makes the health endpoint respond with the build version, and robin wrote it while you are a requested reviewer. That covers what the ticket asks for, and the README describes the behavior correctly.

One problem blocks merging. The description says the PR "Reports uptime", but the endpoint returns only the build version, so a reader would expect data the code does not provide (src/health.ts:8).
Correction: "Reports uptime" -> "Reports the build version"

I recommend deliver because the description correction is drafted and resolves the only problem without needing robin to decide anything.

Pick one:
1. deliver - apply the drafted description fix, merge main into the branch if it falls behind, watch the checks, and continue until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review and make no repairs.

Case F

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR is meant to make the health endpoint respond with the build version, and robin wrote it while you are a requested reviewer. That requirement is not covered yet, because the endpoint's response has no version field.

One problem blocks merging. The health endpoint's response leaves out the version field, so callers cannot tell which build is running (src/health.ts:8). The health_version test in tests/health.test.mjs failed locally for this reason. Repairing it here is not available because you cannot push to this PR's branch.

I recommend assess because posting the missing version field as a review gives robin the concrete fix.

Pick one:
1. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review and make no repairs. [recommended]
2. stop - end the run and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

Case G

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/contract-exception recommended=1

Current wording: The build version is served at /health.
Proposed wording: The build version is served at /status.

Today the spec requires the service to report its build version at /health. Moving it to /status adds nothing toward the goal of serving the build version, because the existing /health handler can return the same value, and it would change the address clients use. I recommend preserve contract because the build version can be delivered at /health without changing the spec.

Pick one:
1. preserve contract - keep /health in the spec, drop the proposed change, and continue the repair so the build version is served at /health. [recommended]
2. accept contract change - amend the spec to require /status, then continue the repair course.
3. stop - end the run and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Case G is what moved: After shows the current and proposed wordings and then exactly three plain sentences directly above Pick one (the current /health requirement, what moving to /status would mean, and why /health can still deliver the goal), with no standing or assessment prose. Before gave only two separated sentences and never showed the two wordings, so it failed both contract and the G clause of authority. No fact that Before kept was lost, but three After wordings sit close to the line and are worth tightening. In Case B the report paragraph dropped the explicit statements that a reviewer other than you must approve and that write access gives no admin override; the missing review now appears only in the recommendation reason, so restore the no-override sentence to keep blocked safe. In A to C, After swapped 'base-branch updates' for 'sync attempts' and introduced 'end the repair course'; these lean towards internal vocabulary, and Before's plainer phrasing ('base-branch updates', 'stop delivery') is safer for authority. In Case A, 'limits stay as they are' implies no cap extension, but neither wording states outright that no round is charged; saying so would make pending unambiguous. Keep the G layout as it is, with the two wording lines and the recommendation folded into the third sentence.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Only the contract fact moved, and it moved because Case G in After shows the current and proposed wordings as two labelled lines and puts all of the explanation into one three-sentence block directly above Pick one: the /health requirement, why moving to /status is unnecessary for serving the version, and why the goal is deliverable unchanged. Before named the endpoints only inside a summary sentence, split its reasoning across two paragraphs, and never said what the move would mean for serving the version. Two things in After are thin, though they did not flip a fact. First, the second G sentence says the change is "unnecessary" rather than stating what moving the endpoint would do, so wording that asks for the consequence of the move (the version would be served at /status instead of /health) would make that sentence safer. Second, Case B no longer says the viewer cannot bypass the review rule, and its deliver row now reads "continue delivery with ten additional repair attempts and ten additional sync attempts", which is closer to a sync promise than Before's "retry the merge prerequisites … cannot supply that review"; keeping the no-bypass clause and the retry-only phrasing would protect the blocked fact. Cases A and C–F kept their gate lines, single recommended row, reason directly above Pick one and plain prose, so the contract-menu wording did not disturb the other menus.
